mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declined over the prior month, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market health that reduces consumer spending confidence, triggering negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rose >0.5pp, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) over two months indicate broad consumer demand contraction that depresses corporate earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS declined, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals aggressive Fed policy that increases equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances meeting FEDFUNDS>2.0% and CPIAUCSL>2.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over two months indicates weakening manufacturing output that lowers corporate profit growth expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declined, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling periods.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales (RSAFS) falling below $390,000 million over the prior month signals reduced consumer spending that depresses corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS < 390000.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and declines in employment (PAYEMS) over one month indicate labor market deterioration that reduces household income and consumer spending, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rose and PAYEMS declined, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year periods.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) over two months signal severe economic contraction that lowers corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declined and UNRATE rose, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
